raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

Make multimodal CUDA VMM transport opt-in, just like CUDA IPC. An unset
`--mm-feature-transport` now resolves to CPU on every topology, including
GB200/GB300 with IMEX. Explicit GPU transports and the deprecated IPC env opt-in
remain supported.

This avoids automatically reserving a GPU feature pool and exposing deployments
to the pool-full GPU-to-CPU fallback reported in #43402. Thanks to @StarDuster
for the report and native-stack evidence. The lifecycle fixes from #43475 are
already on main; **this is a safe-default mitigation, not a fix for the unresolved
CUDA D2H hang**, and must not close #43402.

Update CLI help, the K3 command picker, K3/GLM cookbooks and common VLM guidance:
the transport pool budget is not a GPU preprocessing peak-memory limit. Main
already accounts for the pool in the KV budget. CPU transport does not force
CPU-only decoding/preprocessing and can cost transfer latency; GPU transport is
still available for deployments that explicitly choose and validate it.

## Validation

- Original main + new regression: GB200/GB300 with IMEX both fail the intended
  CPU-default assertion. These are mocked topology-selection tests, not a real
  MNNVL deployment.
- Dedicated B200, driver 580.126.09, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0:
  430 unit tests + 206 subtests passed with CUDA hidden; 6 real CUDA IPC
  cross-process/lifecycle tests passed.
- Real-weight Qwen3.5-2B: default CPU and explicit IPC both start, expose the
  expected resolved setting, and answer four alternating/repeated red/blue image
  requests correctly (8 requests total). Both servers shut down; GPU use returned
  to 0 MiB. IPC teardown printed a PyTorch shared-tensor warning; this smoke does
  not establish long-running IPC/VMM lifetime correctness.
- Pre-commit, cookbook config validation, Mintlify build and broken-links passed.
  The build reports six warnings on unchanged pages.

Not validated: full K3, multi-node MNNVL/EPD, performance, or the incident's
aarch64/580.126.20 hang. The existing 15-case VMM GPU suite requires at least three
GPUs and was skipped on this one-GPU allocation.

 All strategies enable multimodal serving. Image and video input use `Glm5NextProcessor`, which the pinned Transformers release ships (the MI355X checks predate that release and used commit `e4052f55`). On MI355X, text, image, and an image-bearing follow-up were qualified with that build; video was not evaluated. The processor samples video at 2 FPS and caps video input at 240,000 visual tokens. Install `torchcodec` in the serving environment before sending video requests. For very long videos on 4x GB300, use encoder disaggregation to isolate the vision encoder's memory spikes from language decoding.
 
-The default multimodal feature transport is automatic, and on a single CUDA node auto resolves to CPU transport. The MI355X selection explicitly emits CPU transport, matching its image-serving check. CUDA IPC is opt-in: pass `--mm-feature-transport cuda_ipc` when lower transfer latency matters more than the GPU memory the IPC pool reserves. CUDA VMM transport applies only to multi-node GB200/GB300 systems on the MNNVL fabric, where auto selects it.
+Multimodal features use CPU transport by default, including on multi-node GB200/GB300. The MI355X selection explicitly emits CPU transport, matching its image-serving check. CUDA IPC and VMM are opt-in: use `--mm-feature-transport cuda_ipc` on one CUDA node, or `cuda_vmm` with configured MNNVL/IMEX for cross-node sharing. These pools consume additional HBM; benchmark before enabling them. The pool budget does not cap GPU preprocessing peak memory. See [VLM transport guidance](/docs/supported-models/multimodal_language_models#performance-optimization).

@@ -409,12 +409,25 @@ sglang serve \
 
 ### Performance Optimization
 
-For multimodal models, you can use `--mm-feature-transport=cuda_ipc` to optimize for latency at the cost of increased GPU memory usage:
-
-- **Default behavior**: Multimodal feature tensors are moved to CPU after processing to save GPU memory
-- **With `--mm-feature-transport=cuda_ipc`**: Feature tensors stay in a bounded GPU pool shared over CUDA IPC, reducing device-to-host copy overhead and improving latency, but consuming more GPU memory
-
-Use this option when you have sufficient GPU memory and want to minimize latency for multimodal inference.
+Multimodal feature transport defaults to CPU on every topology. GPU transports
+are opt-in and trade additional HBM usage for potentially lower transfer latency:
+
+- `--mm-feature-transport=cpu`: No GPU feature pool. Use this explicitly on older
+  builds or to override the legacy `SGLANG_USE_CUDA_IPC_TRANSPORT=1` opt-in.
+- `--mm-feature-transport=cuda_ipc`: A bounded GPU pool shared within one CUDA node.
+- `--mm-feature-transport=cuda_vmm`: A bounded GPU pool; cross-node sharing requires
+  configured MNNVL/IMEX and a supported model.
+
+`SGLANG_MM_FEATURE_CACHE_MB` limits the GPU transport pool (default 1024 MiB,
+shared across tokenizer workers on the base GPU), **not total GPU preprocessing
+memory**. GPU decode and preprocessing can allocate temporary tensors outside
+this pool; CPU transport does not force these stages onto CPU. A full GPU pool
+falls back to CPU transport per tensor. If you encounter pool-exhaustion hangs
+such as [#43402](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/43402), use CPU
+transport; increasing the pool is not a fix for a leak or a blocked CUDA copy.
+
+Benchmark before opting into GPU transport. This flag does not control EPD
+encoder-output transfer or PD KV transfer.
